fine_trace.note: While parsing the quoted JSCOMPS parameter value of the attacker-controlled vCard property, each ';' byte inside the quotes falls through to the default case and is copied into state->buf (semicolons are preserved inside quotes for structured parameters).
When the parameter is terminated by ':', the accumulated value string containing all 21 ';' separators is passed as the parameter value.
The JSCOMPS parameter has value_kind VCARD_STRUCTURED_VALUE, so the raw value string (with its 21 ';' characters) is forwarded unchanged to vcardstructured_new_from_string.

vcardstructured_alloc() allocates exactly sizeof(struct vcardstructuredtype_impl) (176 bytes), whose field[] member has a fixed capacity of VCARD_MAX_STRUCTURED_FIELDS (20) pointers; str points at the semicolon-laden value.
The first field is stored at index 0; every ';' in the value appends another field the same way, so num_fields grows by one per semicolon.

For each of the 21 ';' characters a new field is allocated and st->num_fields incremented with no check against VCARD_MAX_STRUCTURED_FIELDS (20); the safety condition st->num_fields < VCARD_MAX_STRUCTURED_FIELDS should have held before each append.

On the 21st ';' (st->num_fields == 20) the write targets st->field[20], 8 bytes past the fixed 20-element field[] array at the end of the 176-byte heap allocation: heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 8.
